title.narrative: NIHR Global Health Centre for Multiple Long Term Conditions

description.narrative: The Centre aims to: (i) improve care for people living with MLTC in both countries by co-designing, implementing and evaluating a contextually relevant, patient-centred, equity promoting, simple technology leveraged innovative health system intervention and (ii) strengthen national health research systems by capacity building, creating networks of MLTC researchers and key stakeholders, using ‘systems’ (individual, institutional and environments) thinking.

The NIHR Global Health Centre for Multiple Long Term Conditions is collaborative centre for excellence jointly led by the University of Leicester and Public Health Foundation of India, with two further collaborators in India (HRIDAY, Delhi and AIIMS Jodhpur) and one in Nepal (Kathmandu Medical College), with a remit of conducting high-quality research and building research capacity of the LMIC members in the area of multiple long term conditions.
The target groups are people living with multiple long term conditions in both rural and urban areas in India and Nepal

participating-org.narrative: All India Institute of Medical Sciences Jodhpur
National Institute of Health and Care Excellence

activity-date.narrative: The Centre is currently funded for 5 years, so the current planned end date is 30/09/2027

sector.narrative: Approximately 50% of the Global Health Research Centre's activities and resources will be devoted to conducting high quality research into the treatment and management of those living with multiple long-term conditions in India and Nepal, with a specific focus on chronic and non-communicable diseases.

Approximately 50% of the Global Health Research Centre's activities and resources will be devoted to training and capacity building activities for staff and students affiliated with the LMIC institutions based in India and Nepal. This will include a broad variety of short- and long-form training courses, including MSc/MRes and PhD studentships and short courses for a wide variety of University staff. The primary aim of these activities will be build capacity for these individuals and institutions to support or deliver high quality healthcare research in the future
